chunks: The arrogant will say to the weak: 'Did we hold you back from guidance after it had come to you? Certainly not. In fact you were yourselves guilty.'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفُونَ: The weak, those who were oppressed or humble
key_terms.الْمُسْتَكْبِرُونَ: The arrogant, those who exalted themselves

ai.seo_question: Who are the arrogant and the weak in the context of the Day of Judgment according to Surah Saba?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Saba, the arrogant leaders (al-mustakbirun) attempt to shift blame to the weak (al-mustad'afun) by claiming they obstructed their path to guidance, but the weak refute this by asserting their own free will and the leaders' inherent guilt. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, highlight this as a key moment of accountability where the 'weak' are not merely passive victims but active participants who chose disbelief despite available guidance. This interaction underscores the principle of individual responsibility (taklif) while critiquing the psychological deflection used by the elite to avoid divine judgment.
